key_insight: A two-stage CNN-LSTM plus offline reinforcement learning framework can correct residual trajectory errors and substantially improve continuous 3D EEG motor-imagery decoding.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical post-processing layer for brain-computer interfaces, improving accuracy without requiring additional neural input or changes to the base decoder.
method: Train a CNN-LSTM to decode continuous 3D kinematics from EEG.
Apply an offline RL agent to predicted trajectories to learn residual corrections toward target motion.
Evaluate decoding quality with correlation (r) and RMSE across 2D and VR settings.
evidence_signal: Compared with CNN-LSTM alone, CNN-LSTM-RL increased mean correlation to 0.7181 in 2D and 0.7780 in VR while reducing RMSE to 0.0532 and 0.0441, with statistically significant gains.
watch_item: The RL correction is trained offline on predicted trajectories, so performance may depend on how well the training distribution matches new users, sessions, and task conditions.
paper_title: Learning Residual Kinematic Corrections for Continuous Neural Decoding via Reinforcement Learning
